title: Domain-wall structure and controlled collision
question: Does the canonical coherence PDE support resolved traveling domain walls whose controlled collision remains bounded, conservative, constraint-compatible, dimensionally embeddable, and free of a growing grid-scale cascade?
prediction: Five wall-pair evolutions collide with minimum separation below two units, remain bounded, conserve vacuum-subtracted energy within 2e-10, retain their two walls after collision, agree under planar 2D and 3D embedding, and show decreasing high-wavenumber fraction across the finest 1D resolutions.
falsifier: A missed collision, amplitude-limit violation, energy or reduction-constraint failure, unresolved incoming speed, dimensional mismatch, increasing high-wavenumber pileup, or an unpredicted change in wall count falsifies the registered regime.
controls: The wall and antiwall interpolate between the two analytic condensed vacua on a periodic domain.
The initial momentum is the Lorentz-boosted inward wall profile; subsequent motion comes only from the canonical scalar RHS.
Vacuum energy is subtracted before the conserved collision energy is compared.
The independently evolved three-component scalar gradient is retained and its reduction constraint is measured.
The collision is repeated at three longitudinal resolutions.
Two- and three-dimensional runs use exactly homogeneous transverse embeddings as dimensional controls.
The high-wavenumber energy fraction is compared across the two finest resolutions to detect grid-scale pileup.
seed_rationale: The analytic wall pair, boost, grids, and evolution are deterministic.
